question: m10
q: Is the Friday dip as big for suburban morning commuters as it is for the CBD?

transcript.answer:
**Roughly as big, and in suburbs (all modes) slightly bigger.** The two series measure different things, so this is an approximate comparison.

- **Sydney CBD (3–7pm, people leaving work):** Friday taps are 0.783 of the Tue–Thu average in September 2026. Averaged over the last 12 months (Oct 2025–Sep 2026) the ratio is about 0.775, so Friday evening volume is roughly 22–23% lower than midweek.
- **Suburbs (7–9am, people leaving home), last 12 months:**
  - All modes: 0.758, so Friday morning volume is about 24% lower than midweek.
  - Bus only: 0.799, so about 20% lower, close to the CBD figure.

The suburban dip has also deepened more since before COVID. Pre-COVID, suburban all-mode morning taps were 0.933 on Fridays, a dip of about 7%. The CBD was about 0.885 in January–March 2020 (its latest figure of 0.783 is a similar move of about 10 points). So the suburban drop has been larger in proportion, from a much smaller starting dip.

Caveats:
- The CBD and suburban figures cover different time windows and directions, so this is not a like-for-like comparison.
- The suburban series is everything outside the named centres, so it blends many different areas.
- The CBD pre-COVID baseline is a Jan–Mar 2020 average, not a full-year figure.
